source_name: Zakon o platnom prometu Crne Gore — consolidated text (CBCG PDF)
why_relevant: The statute that defines what a payment institution and an e-money institution are, which activities require a licence, and which reporting obligations generate the public statistics. PSD2-aligned amendments (in force 8 October, per reporting) introduced account information services and payment initiation services as licensable categories — the legal basis for the AISP/PISP entries visible in the register. Essential for interpreting register categories correctly.

source_name: PaySpot ME d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site
why_relevant: Licensed payment institution self-describing as a leader in Montenegrin payment services; publishes service catalogue, point-of-service network and roadmap (domestic and international money transfers, marketplace payments for legal entities and entrepreneurs, e-commerce, digital channels). Own-published coverage and pricing quantify non-bank payment flows at the retail counter level.

source_name: Moneta MNE d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site (MoneyGram principal agent)
why_relevant: Licensed payment institution specialised in fast money transfer and the MoneyGram representative in Montenegro, reported at 100+ service locations nationwide. Its location list and tariffs are the best available proxy for remittance-channel coverage and pricing outside the banking licence.

source_name: Montenegro Transfers d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site (Western Union agent)
why_relevant: Reported as the first payment institution registered in Montenegro (2015) and the Western Union agent; owned within the Alta group (search results also attribute 100% ownership to Eki Transfers — ownership claims conflict and need verification). Publishes Western Union send tariffs for Montenegro, giving direct outbound-remittance pricing data.

source_name: Alta Pay Group d.o.o. Podgorica — Montenegro operation (Alta Pay / AltaPay group)
why_relevant: Licensed payment institution (founded Podgorica, October 2019) running a bill-payment point network across Montenegro: EPCG electricity, internet and cable TV, Ministry of Interior fees, CRPS fees, cadastre, residence tax and school fees, plus payments for legal entities. Group-level communications report revenue multiples and expansion, and the group is linked to Alta banka — making it the clearest case of a payment institution converging on banking. The Montenegro-facing presence is partly on Facebook rather than a dedicated .me site, which weakens machine-collectability.

source_name: PrestoPay d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site and blog
why_relevant: Licensed payment institution positioning itself as the first in Montenegro licensed under the PSD2-aligned framework, offering a multibanking mobile app (account aggregation across Montenegrin banks) and 'Presto Link'. Its published Opšti uslovi poslovanja (general terms of business for payment services) and its bank-connection instruction pages effectively enumerate which Montenegrin banks expose open-banking/AISP interfaces — a rare, otherwise unpublished datum.

source_name: Pošta Crne Gore — Usluge novčanog poslovanja (postal money services)
why_relevant: The national post is the largest physical non-bank payment counter network in Montenegro and acts as agent for Western Union, Ria Money Transfer and MoneyGram simultaneously. Its service and tariff pages quantify counter-based cash payment and remittance access, including in municipalities with no bank branch — directly relevant to cash-usage and coverage analysis.

source_name: Western Union Montenegro — agent locator and country site
why_relevant: Scheme-side view of Montenegro's remittance payout network. The agent list observed via secondary reporting spans Pošta Crne Gore, Adriatic Bank, CKB, Erste, Hipotekarna, Komercijalna, Lovćen, Podgorička, Prva, UCB, Ziraat, the mobile operator MTEL, and bus stations in Podgorica, Nikšić, Herceg Novi, Sutomore, Tivat and Cetinje — evidence that non-bank and telco channels sit alongside banks in the payout mix. Locator pages on this domain are commonly bot-defended, so expect friction.

source_name: CRPS — Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (Montenegro company register and search portal)
why_relevant: The corporate-identity backbone for this cell: registration data, legal form, activity code (payment institutions register under monetary-intermediation codes), ownership and filed financial statements for every licensed payment institution and its agents. It is how you convert a bare register name like 'Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o.' into a real actor with owners and revenue, and how you resolve conflicting ownership claims (e.g. Montenegro Transfers).

source_name: UNDP Montenegro — Procjena regulatornog okvira za razvoj FinTech industrije u Crnoj Gori
why_relevant: Donor-funded assessment of Montenegro's fintech regulatory framework — the kind of document that names the actual market participants, quantifies barriers to e-money and payment licensing, and explains why the e-money register is empty. Provides baseline context and a likely bibliography of further local sources. Dated 2022, so treat figures as historical.

source_name: Investitor.me — Montenegrin business and finance portal
why_relevant: Business daily that tracks ownership and strategy moves among non-bank payment players — observed headline (August 2026) on the Alta group owner expanding into Montenegro via Addiko, and 2022 coverage of the PSD2-aligned Zakon o platnom prometu entering into force. Good for M&A and payment-institution-to-bank convergence signals.

source_name: CBCG — Nadzor u oblasti sprječavanja pranja novca i finansiranja terorizma (AML/CFT supervision)
why_relevant: Payment institutions, e-money issuers and money-remittance agents are AML-supervised obliged entities. This section carries supervisory priorities, guidance and, where published, enforcement outcomes — a channel that reveals the risk profile and sometimes the operational scale of remittance and cash-heavy non-bank payment actors that publish nothing themselves.

source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema (Register of Payment Systems)
why_relevant: Enumerates the authorised payment systems operating in Montenegro and their operators. Determines which clearing and settlement rails non-bank payment institutions can access (directly or only via a sponsoring bank), which is the structural constraint on how large their flows can get.

source_name: Mastercard Crna Gora — MasterIndex istraživanje (annual Montenegro cardholder survey)
source_subtype: card scheme country site / recurring market survey
why_relevant: MasterIndex is a Montenegro-specific consumer payment survey run annually since 2009 by Mastercard, publishing card ownership penetration (e.g. debit card ownership share), usage-by-merchant-category splits, contactless adoption and motivations for card vs cash. It is one of very few sources giving demand-side card behaviour statistics for ME that are not central-bank aggregates.

source_name: Mastercard Crna Gora — novosti / vizija section (country newsroom)
why_relevant: Country-level Mastercard news hub carrying first-in-market milestone announcements (Google Pay Montenegro, contactless, tokenisation, issuer/acquirer additions). Milestone releases date the diffusion of payment technology in ME and name which banks moved first.

source_name: Mastercard Serbia site — Montenegro-tagged releases (mastercard.rs)
why_relevant: Mastercard's regional Serbian-language site also hosts Montenegro-specific announcements (e.g. Google Pay launch in Crna Gora), meaning ME milestone news is split across two domains — a collection trap if only mastercard.me is monitored.

source_name: Visa Southeast Europe — Montenegro country page
why_relevant: Visa's dedicated SEE regional site with a Montenegro entry point; the scheme's country presence page and gateway to product/market positioning for ME. Useful as the anchor for Visa-side milestone tracking and to identify the ME issuer/acceptance footprint Visa itself advertises.

source_name: Visa Southeast Europe Newsroom
why_relevant: The regional Visa press channel where SEE/Montenegro milestone releases and any Visa-generated spend/tourism data for the region would be announced. Visa tourism-spend commentary is one of the few cross-border card-spend indicators available for a tourism-dependent economy like ME.

source_name: Visa corporate — Visa Perspectives / trends & insights (CEMEA regional economic outlook)
why_relevant: Visa's own regional commentary combines cardholder spend data with tourism economics for CEMEA/SEE; Montenegro appears as part of the regional narrative rather than a standalone dataset, but supplies scheme-authored context and occasionally country-level figures.

source_name: Payten (Asseco SEE) — News & Events, Montenegro implementations
why_relevant: Payten's news feed names the exact Montenegrin banks running its estates — the SoftPOS implementation at Hipotekarna banka is a concrete supplier-to-bank link. This is the core supplier-ecosystem route that bypasses the absence of public procurement disclosure by private ME banks, and it dates technology rollouts (SoftPOS, Android POS, cash recyclers).

source_name: Asseco Case Study Book — Payment chapter
why_relevant: Curated Asseco group case-study repository organised by domain; payment chapter entries identify named client banks and the scale of deployments (terminal/ATM counts, processing volumes) across SEE including ME. Case studies frequently disclose estate sizes that banks themselves never publish.

source_name: Asseco South Eastern Europe (ASEE) — annual/management reports (Payment Solutions segment)
why_relevant: Audited, exchange-regulated (WSE) disclosures. The management report explicitly states that POS terminal and ATM maintenance services generate most of the Payment segment's revenue and names Montenegro as one of the most important markets for that business — a rare quantified, third-party-verifiable signal about the size and structure of the ME acquiring/terminal estate. Segment revenue figures are given group-wide with country commentary.

source_name: MoneyGet Crna Gora (Payten independent ATM network, ME)
source_subtype: independent ATM deployer country site / ATM locator
why_relevant: Payten's own independent (non-bank) ATM deployment in Montenegro. Its ATM locator is a de-facto census of the IAD share of the ME ATM fleet — countable, geolocated, and updated — and shows how much of the cash-access network sits outside bank estates. Directly informs cash usage and ATM data topics.
